To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
gated delivery on a Varia linear accelerator equipped with RPM is accurate to within clinically acceptable margins.

gating of the IMRT beam on the Varian Linacs using the RPM system can be performed with clinically acceptable accuracy for a wide range of motion frequencies and gating intervals, and for significant motion amplitude.

the Varian RPM‐based gating system can provide gated dose delivery equivalent to ungated IMRT delivery to within clinically‐acceptable limits, for all clinically‐relevant gating intervals and respiratory frequencies, even in the presence of significant motion amplitude.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the accuracy of gated delivery on the Varian linac.
the accuracy of gated delivery on a Varion Linac equipped with the Real‐Time Management System.
the feasibility of gated delivery on the Varian linac.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RPM system is capable of providing gating accuracy to within clinically acceptable margins for all clinically relevant configurations.
gated IMRT delivery is accurate, and that it is not necessary to use the gating system for the delivery of gated IMRT.
gated IMRT is clinically viable on the Varian linac.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Varian system is capable of accurate gated IMRT delivery for all clinically‐relevant motion frequencies and amplitudes.
gated IMRT delivery using the Varian RPM system is clinically feasible.
gated IMRT delivery is feasible on the Varian linac.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gating can be used to deliver IMRT without significant loss of dose accuracy.
gated IMRT delivery is accurate and reliable, and should be used with confidence.
gating can be performed with high accuracy, even with the RPM system, and that gating is feasible with motion amplitudes and frequencies that are likely to be encountered clinically.
